sounds.prompt: a lone woman singing a slow, tender lullaby to a lighthouse lantern, over a soft harp and low sustained strings that play the whole way through
sounds.note: Chapter 2: the Lantern Song, Maren's second song (docs/story/chapter2-script.md), while he binds Beaconwing and under "Chapter 2 complete!" (src/world/chapter2.js, src/ui/battle.js, src/ui/explore.js). Made by hand on 15 October, the third take: one 85 s composition of this plan plus a closing hum section for the keeper's hum (it hummed nothing: that section became the harp's ring-out). Trimmed to 0.1 s before the first harp note; over the 4 s after the chorus (57.2 to 61.2 s) the whole mix eases 5 dB down, so "Goodnight" comes in softly under it; the last chord rings out to silence by 82.7 s, then 1.8 s of quiet (84.5 s in all), so the loop's 3 s crossfade never sings over her goodnight. In the file: verse 4.0 s, Hal's line 23.3 s, chorus 43.0 s, "Goodnight" 61.2 s, her last word held 71.1 to 74.7 s. Its cues are the chorus and "Goodnight": the binding scene starts the chorus as Beaconwing rises and closes the card on the goodnight (src/world/chapter2.js). No keeper's voice: his lips move with her last word (lanternLastLine in the script). Re-making it with --force gives the plan's 75 s without the trim, the softer goodnight or the quiet.

On 17 October the parent said every narrator line sounded very flat: at stability 0.5 with one bland tag in front of a long line he read evenly, so his stability came down to 0.3 like the characters and each line became a whole performance, a lively storyteller tag up front and a tag at each turn.

jumble.name: Library pirate voice
jumble.why: The parent picked it for Captain Jumble, the loud, vain, theatrical ghost-pirate. On Eleven v4 with one tag per line he sounded like an American man, not a pirate, so every line is now a whole performance (tools/audio/direction.json): a tag describing a gravelly, sinister pirate, then a tag at each turn, after the parent's own test of his ending line, 12 October. That test set stability and similarity low, without numbers. v4 takes both as plain numbers, and no v4 preset (like v3's Creative) was found to match, so low here is 0.15 stability, for a freer, more theatrical read, and 0.35 similarity, so the pirate tag can pull him away from the voice's plain read.
